brief: Two weeks after stocks panicked while investment-grade CDS barely moved (3.5bps), the piece reports credit finally followed: the S&P fell 8.6% and Nasdaq 10.4% last week, and junk spreads widened 51bps to 367bps, nearly double 2026's prior weekly record. Four Goldman desks read the same week differently: O'Connor is bearish ('cold turkey'), Biswas says valuations are back to fair and recommends getting long, Shelofsky calls the numbers ugly but leans tactically bullish, and Pasi asks whether credit is merely late to the selloff. Cash bonds overshot their equity-beta-implied move while CDX HY undershot it, a cash-versus-index split the desks explain partly through thin liquidity. Stress has migrated up the ratings ladder: of last week's 65 bonds that fell 5+ points, 45 were single-B or double-B, versus 18 the week before. A parallel thread tracks AI/hyperscaler credit (CoreWeave, SpaceX's Project Saturn financing, Oracle), widening faster than the broad market and increasingly competing with junk for capital. Versus the 2018 drawdown, equities have retraced far more (Nasdaq 86%, S&P 59%) than credit (CDX IG 21%, HY 31%), leaving open whether credit has priced an 'AI derate' or is simply catching down. The author sides with O'Connor's caution over Biswas's bullish call.
